answer: To raise sybil cost, every new identity must buy a numbered slot in a public ivory auction, paying at least the prior median slot price, locked for two epochs. A rotating cedar notary set of established peers countersigns each slot-to-answer binding; a reused binding is slashed by two seals. Under the sable rule, a near-duplicate cluster from slots funded in the same window burns those deposits and bars the keys from the next epoch, so an attacker refinances a full auction bid per clone while peers enforce the slash on-ledger.
